_comment: SHAPE REFERENCE — this is what a project's feature_list.json looks like once features are specified, planned, and built: the full schema-v2 kanban with sub-feature tasks, cross-feature dependencies, phases, evidence, and learning. A real project STARTS EMPTY — /install writes {"schema_version":2,"current_feature":null,"features":{}} to the project root, and grill (WHY/SPECIFY fields) then the lead (PLAN fields) fill it one feature at a time. Two example features below: 'order-totals' is done (passing); 'discount-codes' depends on it and is mid-build. WIP=1, links are reciprocal + acyclic, so validate-board.py accepts it.

order-totals.title: Order total calculation
order-totals.problem_statement: Carts show no running total, so shoppers cannot tell what they will pay before checkout.
order-totals.jtbd: When I add items to my cart, I want to see the order total update, so I can decide whether to keep shopping.
order-totals.user_context: Storefront shoppers on web; high traffic at checkout.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Total equals the sum of line subtotals, rounded once at the end
acceptance_criteria.verification: npm test -- total.spec.ts -t 'sums lines' 2>&1 | grep -q '1 passed'

tasks.title: Sum line subtotals with single final rounding
tasks.context: WHERE: src/cart/total.ts (existing module — extend, do not create a new one). REUSE: src/cart/types.ts:12 `export interface Line { sku: string; qty: number; unitCents: number }` and src/cart/types.ts:24 `export const roundHalfUp = (cents: number): number => Math.round(cents)` — round ONCE at the end, never per line. EXEMPLAR: src/cart/tax.ts:1-40 — same pure-function + integer-cents shape this repo uses for money. INTERFACES: `export function orderTotal(lines: Line[]): number` — cents in, cents out; never floats. CONNECTS: called from src/api/checkout.ts:88 (already imports `orderTotal`); no other call sites. CONVENTIONS: named exports only; throw `RangeError` on a negative qty (the repo never returns error codes). TEST: src/cart/total.spec.ts -> 'sums line subtotals with a single final rounding' — RED command: npm test -- total.spec.ts. BEHAVIOR: lines [{qty:3,unitCents:333},{qty:1,unitCents:1}] -> 1000 (3*333 + 1 = 1000; rounding applied once, not per line).

validation.business_metric: line-sum match verified on 1000 sampled carts

product: shoppers expect the total before, not at, checkout

discount-codes.title: Discount code application
discount-codes.problem_statement: Marketing cannot run promotions because the cart has no way to apply a discount code.
discount-codes.jtbd: When I have a promo code, I want to apply it at the cart, so I can get the advertised discount.
discount-codes.user_context: Shoppers with codes from email campaigns; codes are percentage or fixed-amount.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A valid percentage code reduces the total by that percent of the pre-discount total
A valid fixed code reduces the total by the fixed amount, never below zero
An unknown or expired code is rejected and leaves the total unchanged

tasks.title: Parse + validate a discount code (known/expired/unknown)
tasks.context: WHERE: src/cart/discount.ts (new module beside src/cart/total.ts). REUSE: src/cart/types.ts:31 `export interface DiscountCode { code: string; kind: 'percent' | 'fixed'; value: number; expiresAt: string }` and src/cart/clock.ts:7 `export const now = (): Date => new Date()` — take time from `now()`, never construct a clock inline. EXEMPLAR: src/cart/coupon.ts:1-52 — the same parse -> validate -> typed-result shape. INTERFACES: `export type ParsedCode = { ok: true; code: DiscountCode } | { ok: false; reason: 'unknown' | 'expired' }`; `export function parseCode(raw: string, table: DiscountCode[]): ParsedCode`. CONNECTS: nothing imports it yet — T2 wires it into total.ts. CONVENTIONS: exhaustive switch on `kind`; no `any`; comparisons are case-insensitive on `code`. TEST: src/cart/discount.spec.ts -> 'parse rejects an expired code' — RED command: npm test -- discount.spec.ts -t 'parse'. BEHAVIOR: 'SAVE10' present with expiresAt in the past -> { ok:false, reason:'expired' }; absent -> { ok:false, reason:'unknown' }.

tasks.title: Apply percentage discount to the order total
tasks.context: WHERE: src/cart/discount.ts (percentage branch) + the single call site in src/cart/total.ts. REUSE: src/cart/types.ts:24 `roundHalfUp`; T1's `parseCode` (same module) — do not re-validate the code here. EXEMPLAR: src/cart/tax.ts:22-38 — how a percentage is applied to integer cents in this repo. INTERFACES: `export function applyDiscount(totalCents: number, parsed: ParsedCode): number`. CONNECTS: src/cart/total.ts:41 — `orderTotal` returns its sum through `applyDiscount` when a code is present. CONVENTIONS: percentage math in integer cents, `roundHalfUp` applied once, at the end. TEST: src/cart/discount.spec.ts -> 'percentage discount rounds half up' — RED command: npm test -- discount.spec.ts -t 'percentage'. BEHAVIOR: total 1999 + SAVE10 (percent, 10) -> 1799 (199.9 rounds half-up to 200).

tasks.title: Apply fixed-amount discount with a zero floor
tasks.context: WHERE: src/cart/discount.ts (fixed-amount branch only — do not touch the percentage branch). REUSE: T1's `ParsedCode` + T2's `applyDiscount` signature (same module); no new helper is needed. EXEMPLAR: the percentage branch T2 adds — mirror its structure exactly. INTERFACES: unchanged — the fixed case is a branch inside `applyDiscount`. CONNECTS: no new call site. CONVENTIONS: clamp with `Math.max(0, ...)`; never return a negative total. TEST: src/cart/discount.spec.ts -> 'fixed floor never goes below zero' — RED command: npm test -- discount.spec.ts -t 'fixed floor'. BEHAVIOR: total 500 + a fixed 800 code -> 0 (floored), not -300.
